channel.title: Veille IA et cybersécurité — Yuung Kansietoko
channel.description: Articles sur l'intelligence artificielle dans la cybersécurité et failles exploitées liées à l'IA, agrégés toutes les heures depuis The Hacker News, BleepingComputer, Dark Reading, SecurityWeek, Le Monde Informatique, Embrace The Red, Simon Willison, le CERT-FR et la CISA.

item.title: [SecurityWeek] OpenAI Unveils Daybreak Red Team, Defense Factory Security Tools
item.description: Daybreak Red Team pentests web applications with AI agents, while Defense Factory investigates security findings and prepares patches. The post OpenAI Unveils Daybreak Red Team, Defense Factory Security Tools appeared first on SecurityWeek .

item.title: [Le Monde Informatique] Cybersécurité : OpenAI enrichit Daybreak de deux outils d’IA pour traquer les failles
item.description: OpenAI étoffe sa plateforme de cybersécurité Daybreak avec deux solutions reposant sur des agents d’intelligence artificielle. Présentés le 12 novembre 2026, Daybreak Red Team et Daybreak Defense Factory visent respectivement à automatiser les tests d’intrusion et à accélérer la préparation des…

item.title: [Dark Reading] Cyber Experts Weigh In: How to Fight Artex & AntiFox
item.description: Cybercriminals using agentic pen-testing tools is a proverbial genie out of the bottle at this point, so enterprises need to get a defense plan in place right away.

item.title: [BleepingComputer] Massive Microsoft 365 outage disrupts Outlook, Teams, Copilot worldwide
item.description: Microsoft is investigating a widespread outage affecting multiple Microsoft 365 services, including Outlook, Microsoft Teams, and Copilot, as users report connectivity problems worldwide. [...]

item.title: [SecurityWeek] Apache Patches Critical HTTP Server RCE Found by Anthropic, Google
item.description: The mod_http2 race condition, CVE-2026-119618, could let unauthenticated attackers execute code on servers with HTTP/2 enabled. The post Apache Patches Critical HTTP Server RCE Found by Anthropic, Google appeared first on SecurityWeek .

item.title: [The Hacker News] 186 Fake AI Domains Redirect Users to ClickFix Lures, Browser Malware, and Search Hijackers
item.description: Cybersecurity researchers have found that lookalike domains masquerading as artificial intelligence (AI) tools are being used to serve ClickFix-style lures, browser-hijacking malware, and a set of extensions that hijack user searches. This delivery pattern has been codenamed TypoPrompting by…

item.title: [Dark Reading] Inside an AI Attack Against a US Retailer
item.description: When hand-typed commands failed to breach a US retailer, the attacker turned to AI-generated scripts, achieving lateral movement in minutes.

item.title: [Le Monde Informatique] Grok Build : plus de 35 000 applications IA accessibles sans authentification
item.description: Une étude de la société de cybersécurité Claroc révèle d’importants défauts de confidentialité dans des applications créées avec Grok Build, l’outil de création d’applications assistée par IA de SpaceXSI, l’éditeur de Grok anciennement appelé xAI. Sur les 37 571 applications actives examinées, 35…

item.title: [Dark Reading] Chinese AI Project Scouts Spies in Taiwan Chip Industry
item.description: The CCP built a Big Data system to scrape reams of information and learn about individuals abroad, to potentially target and exploit them. Think Alice Huang Lite.

item.title: [Dark Reading] Japan Pushes Emergency Funding for Cybersecurity as AI-Assisted Breaches Rise
item.description: The package adds public-private cyber responders, an AI-focused team run by the economic ministry, and more leeway to use the government's new active cyber-defense powers.

item.title: [Dark Reading] AI Raises the Stakes for Cyber Resilience
item.description: An organization's ability to quickly recover from a business disruption will be a competitive advantage in an era of AI-driven threats and business enablement.

item.title: [The Hacker News] AntiFox AI Pentesting Platform Linked to Attacks That Accessed AWS Production Secrets
item.description: Cybersecurity researchers have disclosed details of a campaign in which an emerging agentic penetration testing platform called AntiFox has been used to steal Amazon Web Services (AWS) credentials and pivot laterally into compromised environments. "In several recently observed intrusions, Alibaba…

item.title: [The Hacker News] Over 35,000 Grok-Built Apps Exposed Online, Some Leaking Confidential Data and Passwords
item.description: Of the 37,571 Grok-built apps that security company Claroc found online, 35,578 were open to anyone without a sign-in, the researchers said yesterday. They included 24 apps built by staff at the social network X and at SpaceXSI, the company that makes the Grok AI assistant. Most of the open apps…

item.title: [The Hacker News] We Built An Agent That Broke All of Our Security Rules. Here's What We Learned.
item.description: We tell customers three things about securing AI agents: they need their own identities, access that fits the job they’re given, and traceability that’s separate from any human’s. That was true for us at Token as well. Then, we built an agent that broke all three by default. This helped us think…

item.title: [The Hacker News] Railway Says Stolen Customer AI Keys Led to $740,000 in Estimated Unauthorized Usage Charges
item.description: AI provider keys that customers stored on Railway were stolen in an October breach and used to commit an estimated $740,000 in unauthorized spending, the platform-as-a-service provider said yesterday. It has promised to pay those charges itself when an AI provider will not refund them. The company…

item.title: [The Hacker News] Microsoft Researchers Show AI Agents Can Be Backdoored by Editing Fewer Than 10 Neurons
item.description: An AI model can be given a hidden backdoor by editing fewer than 10 of its rarely used neurons, without retraining the model, Microsoft researchers have shown. When a chosen trigger appears, the model outputs an attacker's command, which an agent using that model would run with the agent's own…

item.title: [Dark Reading] Artex: The AI Pen-Test Tool Hackers Turned Into a Weapon
item.description: Forks of the open source Artex framework, along with 45 similar pen-testing tools, remain capable of executing credential attacks and cloud breaches at machine speed across multiple industries.

item.title: [Dark Reading] F-Secure Identifies 26 Ways AI Can Harm Consumers, and Where to Stop Them
item.description: New AI Harms Taxonomy traces how harm moves through AI systems, from misleading chatbot answers to compromised autonomous agents, and identifies where defenses can intervene.

item.title: [Dark Reading] Checkmarx Appoints Kobi Sivilya as Chief Information Security Officer
item.description: Sivilya brings deep cybersecurity and technology leadership to Checkmarx as AI transforms software development.

item.title: [The Hacker News] SGLang RCE Exploit Breaches NEAR AI, Steals Data From 18 Agents and About 100 Users
item.description: An attacker exploited a remote code execution flaw in SGLang, an open-source inference engine, and ran code on one of NEAR AI's inference servers last Sunday. The attacker could also have seen requests being processed on that server that day, including requests sent in confidential mode, the…

item.title: [Dark Reading] AI Coding Agents Leak Thousands of Secrets to GitHub
item.description: A command in Claude Code inadvertently saves files with credentials and other sensitive data to public Git repositories, creating security gaps for organizations.

item.title: [The Hacker News] Fireworks AI Confirms Wider Breach Affecting Customer Datasets, Model Weights and Notion AI Chats
item.description: Fireworks AI disclosed on Monday that its investigation into a security incident first reported early last month uncovered further malicious activity, affecting account and billing information, alongside secrets, datasets, and incomplete models for a "limited set of accounts." In a notice published…

item.title: [Dark Reading] AI Makes Reverse Engineering Mainstream Software & Malware Far Easier
item.description: Researchers unpacked, mapped, and recreated complex software and the Turla malware, raising opportunities and concerns for organizations and cybersecurity analysts.

item.title: [Le Monde Informatique] Cisco et IBM vont intégrer Mythos à leurs outils de cybersécurité
item.description: Cisco et IBM préparent l’intégration de Claude Mythos dans leurs produits de sécurité. Le premier utilisera le modèle d’Anthropic pour renforcer les tests offensifs des systèmes d’IA. Le second vise la détection et la correction de vulnérabilités logicielles. Ces projets élargissent l’accès aux…

item.title: [The Hacker News] Anthropic's Claude Fable 5.2 Beats GPT-6 Cyber in Multi-Stage Cyberattack Benchmark
item.description: Anthropic on Monday released Claude Fable 5.2 and Claude Mythos 5.2 models, which it said exhibit improvements in coding, reasoning, and vision. During pre-release training, the large language models (LLMs) helped its engineers "complete otherwise-infeasible software migrations, designed three…

item.title: [Dark Reading] People Are Getting Weird About AI
item.description: Dark Reading Confidential Episode 22: You can love AI without being blind to cybersecurity being sacrificed for utility. The tendency for humans to anthropomorphize the conversations and interactions we're having with AI is growing into potential delusion.

item.title: [Dark Reading] Attackers Crash Claude's 'Office Party' Flaw to Run Malicious Code on Linux
item.description: Attackers can exploit a flaw in Claude's document-processing tool by creating a temporary file that Anthropic's AI assistant can access and run on a user's machine.

item.title: [Dark Reading] PwC's CISO on AI, Robots & What's Next for Security
item.description: As AI accelerates change across the enterprise, PwC's James Shira explains why security teams must rethink their approach to risk and adapt their strategies.

item.title: [Dark Reading] UK Wades Into Tech Sovereignty Amid AI Policy Changes
item.description: The UK is betting on domestic AI and cyber investment to reduce reliance on US tech — but security leaders question whether the funding is too fragmented and too late.

item.title: [Dark Reading] AI Gave Your Incident Archive a Second Job
item.description: Security records are increasingly being used by vendors to train their models, creating new risks for enterprises.

item.title: [Dark Reading] UK Warns Its Critical Infrastructure Faces Grave Risk
item.description: Britain's new Labour-led government is making a concerted push to get ahead of the AI risks to its national networks and the industrial complex.

item.title: [Dark Reading] SecurityDataPipeline.com Launches as a New Educational Resource for the AI Era
item.description: The ungated resource explains how security data pipelines reduce SIEM ingestion costs, preserve detection coverage, and prepare the data layer for AI-driven security operations.

item.title: [Dark Reading] LLMjacking Emerges as Thriving Cybercriminal Enterprise
item.description: Cybercriminals have turned reselling cloud access to LLMs into a lucrative business model, with some victims paying as much as $1 million in resource consumption before access was revoked.

item.title: [Dark Reading] 3AM Affiliate Embraces AI-Like Loops in European School Attack
item.description: Evidence suggests a model may have generated and revised commands during the ransom gang's breach, though researchers stopped short of claiming full automation.

item.title: [Dark Reading] Microsoft's AI Risk Report Misses This Key Detail
item.description: The latest "Digital Defense Report" identifies government agencies as prime targets for AI attacks, but it doesn't mention that they are broadly being targeted through Microsoft bugs.

item.title: [Dark Reading] Devs Hit by Trojanized Claude Code Extension for Cursor
item.description: Two serious security issues hit Cursor on the same day, highlighting the risks for AI-powered integrated development environments (IDEs).
